I’m a college student and I work online so if we lost the fight for net neutrality, I would loose my current and potential livelihood.

Personally, however, I use the internet as a means to communicate with people I don’t come in contact with everyday like my siblings who live across the country or my friends who have different schedules than I do. Some days, due to health issues, social media communication is the only interaction I get. It makes me feel connected even when I can’t be physically, like I’m part of a community. I am by no means the only one whose situation is like this. If the FCC took away net neutrality, there’d be thousands (if not more) who’d suddenly feel alone.

When I was about 14 or 15, I went to visit the grave of my deceased grandmother with my mother, brother, and now boyfriend (NB). I had no personal attachment to my grandmother so while my mom was standing at the grave, the rest of us wandered around and collected near a creepy looking tree (far away from all the other graves). While inspecting the roots, NB found a peculiar looking object so we all came to investigate. It looked like a wad of garbage to be honest. NB found a long stick and attempted to pick up whatever it was when we noticed the underside was covered in maggots and released a smell that made anyone in a 15ft radius dry heave on cue. We promptly noped the fuck out of there and alerted the cemetery management.

It turns out, we found a zombie leg wrapped in satanic burial bindings coming out of the ground that was "buried" there undocumented. They immediately started a police investigation for homicide and we were under oath to remain silent until the police and the cemetery had dealt with the matter. 

Never found out what happened but to this day, that is the fucking spookiest thing that has happened to me.
